newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs ease on BOJ governor comments.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs ease on BOJ governor comments.

text.p: SIMEX Euroyen and Japanese government bond (JGB) futures subsided on Wednesday, largely due to positive comments about Japan's economy by the Bank of Japan (BOJ) governor Yasuo Matsushita, dealers said.
Matsushita's remark that the economy was improving and that increased confidence could give rise to inflationary fears pushed the December Euroyen down to a low of 99.02 after lunch.
It recovered slightly to 99.04 at 1130 GMT against its IMM close at 99.08.
A trader with a European house said the contract should remain confined to a range of 99.02-99.09 for the time being, with a break below seen dragging it down to 98.95.
"The general feeling is that rates won't change until the autumn so the trend is unchanged," he said.
Vague rumours that Japan's Ministry of Finance might stop its outright JGB purchases also hurt JGB futures, he said. But the MOF denied the rumours.
June JGBs settled at 126.71 against their previous 127.03 after falling as low as 126.55.
"People are still buying JGBs on dips. They should be supported around 126.33/34 and there's more immediate support at 126.62," the trader said.
He said the contract faced resistance around 127.03 after talk of stop-loss buy orders above the 127.10 level failed to materialise.
Eurodollar futures ended slightly higher with the most actively traded December contract at 93.510 against its IMM close at 93.495 on volume of 6,005 lots.
